div.head: CHn cor 5
div.ab: Monetagium commune quod capiebatur per ciuitates et comitatus, quod non fuit tempore regis Eadwardi, hoc ne amodo sit, omnino defendo.
Monetagium commune quod capiebatur per civitates et comitatus, quod non fuit tempore regis Edwardi, hoc ne amodo sit omnino defendo.
I entirely forbid the continuance of the mint-tax levied on cities and counties as against the practice of King Edward's time.

Vgl. Gl Münzänderung; die Ablösung des königlichen Verrufsrechts durch monetagium entstammt Fränk. Wurzel; E. Mayer Dt. Frz. Vfg. I 96 (missverstanden von Freeman Wil. Rufus II 353 und Stubbs Sel. char., Gloss.; Lect. Engl. hist. 112)

Cf. Gl Münzänderung; the commutation of the king’s right of calling in the coinage by monetagium has a Frankish root; E. Mayer Dt. Frz. Vfg. I 96 (misunderstood by Freeman Wil. Rufus II 353 and Stubbs Sel. char., Gloss.; Lect. Engl. hist. 112)
